_README: Copy to config.json and fill in YOUR values, or just run the install wizard (open the folder with Claude Code and say 'install BSF Solar Dispatch' — it asks the questions and writes this for you). This ONE file is the whole system config: the publisher reads it at runtime, and install/deploy.py stamps it into the Node-RED flow + generates the dashboard config. Every default below is roughly a 'typical Australian Victron Cerbo + ~5kW solar + lead-acid + Tuya plugs' setup (≈ the farm it was built on) — installs like that hit Next through most of the wizard; different rigs answer the questions that matter. Keep config.json private (it holds your Tuya keys). _comment keys are ignored. Numeric defaults left as-is reproduce the original tested dispatcher behaviour exactly.
_site_name: Shown in the dashboard header + widget. Make it your place.
_location: Decimal degrees (negative lat = southern hemisphere). Drives sunrise/sunset in the dispatcher + the sun/moon arc on the dashboard. timezone is an IANA name (e.g. Australia/Brisbane, Europe/Berlin).

hardware._vrm_portal_id: Cerbo → Settings → VRM online portal → VRM Portal ID (12 hex). Used read-only for the per-charger MPPT breakdown.
hardware._inverter: Your inverter/charger model + continuous rating in kW (informational + sanity caps).
hardware._fronius: AC-coupled Fronius? present=false if you have none (the Fronius-curtailment signal is then ignored).
hardware._chargers: ONE entry per solar tracker, any count (2/4/6…). kind='solarcharger' for a BlueSolar/SmartSolar MPPT (uses N/<portal>/solarcharger/<instance>/Yield/Power); kind='multi' for a Multi RS PV tracker (uses N/<portal>/multi/<instance>/Pv/<tracker>/P). 'instance' is the VE device instance; 'key' is a short unique id used on the dashboard's per-charger drill-down; 'kw' optional rated size. Find your instances in VRM/Node-RED (victron-input-solarcharger service list).
hardware._inverter_kind: 'victron' (Cerbo GX / Venus OS -- what ships) or 'selectronic' (SP PRO via a Select.live box on the LAN). selectronic swaps the flow's Victron input nodes for MQTT ones fed by publisher/selectlive_bridge.py, and points deploy at a local Node-RED (hardware.nodered_url) instead of the Cerbo.
hardware._nodered_url: Where deploy.py POSTs the flow. Blank = https://<cerbo_ip>:1881 (Cerbo). On a Pi/Selectronic install: http://127.0.0.1:1880
hardware._selectronic: Only when inverter.kind='selectronic'. ip = the Select.live box's LAN address; device_id = the 32-hex id listed at http://<ip>/cgi-bin/solarmonweb/devices/ . Curtailment is synthesised (no MPPT flag on an SP PRO): SOC>=curtail_soc_pct AND |battery_w|<=curtail_batt_w AND solar>=curtail_min_pv_w. mqtt_host = the broker the flow uses (the Pi itself).

battery._chemistry: lead-acid | lifepo4 | lithium-ion. Drives the dashboard SOC colour bands (and is the safety reason the dispatcher keeps SOC high). The wizard auto-fills soc_danger/soc_warn from chemistry: lead-acid 60/75 (must NOT sit low), lifepo4/lithium-ion 20/40. Override if you know your bank. SOC at/below danger = red, below warn = amber, above = green.

solar._total_dc_kw: Total DC array size (sum of your trackers). Informational + scales the curtailment 'forgone kWh' estimate.
solar._curtailment_mode: How the dispatcher decides solar is being throttled: 'auto' (canonical MPPT MppOperationMode if your chargers are wired, else Fronius freq-shift, else SOC heuristic), 'mppt_operation', 'fronius_freq', or 'soc_fallback'. Leave 'auto' unless you know better.

tuya._api_host: Your Tuya cloud data-center endpoint — MUST match the region your Smart Life app account is homed to. See install/region-datacenter-map.md (Australia: usually https://openapi.tuyaeu.com).

_loads: One entry per Tuya plug, ANY count (0–N). Delete the ones you don't have; add more by copying a block. role: hot_water | air_con | inside_temp | well_pump (or any label for extra switched loads — only the four named roles wire into the dispatcher/flow today). device_id from the Tuya portal; local_key+local_ip from `tinytuya wizard` (install/tuya-walkthrough.md §8). rated_w = nameplate watts (used as the metering fallback when the plug isn't reporting live power). essential=true marks a load that shouldn't be treated as discretionary surplus. metered=true = show its live watts on the dashboard.

dispatcher._surplus: surplus_on_w / surplus_off_w = the watts of genuine surplus to turn a load ON / OFF (hysteresis; ON > OFF). surplus_off_w_curt = the lower OFF threshold used while panels are confirmed curtailed. Tune to your array: bigger array → bigger numbers.
dispatcher._curtail_fronius_w: Below this Fronius output (W) the inverter is treated as frequency-shift throttled (a curtailment signal). 50 suits a small AC-coupled Fronius; set higher for a bigger one.
dispatcher._caps: load_cap_w = the most a switched load may add on top of house load (e.g. a circuit/trailer limit). safety_cap_w = hard cascade-trip ceiling (must be ≥ load_cap_w). VERY install-specific — set to YOUR wiring limits.
dispatcher._hw_element_w: Rated draw of your hot-water element (W) — also the metering fallback. Match your element.
dispatcher._sustain: Anti-flap dwell times (ms): a load must see the condition hold this long before it switches. *_curt variants apply while curtailed.
dispatcher._soc_windows: Time-of-day battery SOC gates (on/off %, ON>OFF). W1 (early), W2 (midday), W3 (afternoon) progressively demand a fuller battery before dispatching, so loads run on genuine surplus. Defaults suit lead-acid (keep SOC high). For lithium you can lower these to cycle more.
dispatcher._ac: mode: 'heating' (fire when cold, ON<OFF — what ships) or 'cooling' (fire when hot, ON>OFF). NOTE: choosing 'cooling' flips the dashboard labels + setpoint sense, but the dispatcher's temperature COMPARISON ships in heating mode — true cooling-direction dispatch is a documented manual step (see install/troubleshooting.md → 'Summer cooling'), deliberately not auto-applied to the safety logic. inside_temp_on_c/off_c are the heating setpoints (also tunable live from the dashboard). inside_temp_source: tuya_plug | external | disabled.

display._display: currency/symbol + your electricity price per kWh (for cost readouts). price_per_kwh 0 = hide cost figures.

dashboard._note: The software is free for personal use. tip_url = where the dashboard's ☕buy me a coffee☕ link goes ("" hides it). tip_after_days = days before the one-time thank-you card (0 = never). Display only — never affects dispatch.
dashboard._away_base_url: Optional. The public https address of this site's away view WITHOUT the token, e.g. https://solar-site1.example.com (see install/pi-setup.md section 7). When set, the home-only phone-setup.html page hands the full away link to the widget app so nobody has to type it.
